name: Sipahis
headerMeta: Heroic era · Melee Cavalry (Steel Mace/Blunt) · 215 leadership · T4 · Mastery

origin.text: Blood of the Empire · Heroic Era

pitch: A charge-and-stomp disruptor rather than a killer: Quick Charge leaps knock down and chain into Impassioned for a second wave of knockdowns and a 50% damage-taken debuff, while Croupade grinds out 12 seconds of stomps and stacking defense. It folds instantly against high-damage low-speed anti-cav like Stalwarts and Fortebraccio if you charge into their brace, so it wins by disrupting shielded infantry and simple cavalry matchups, not by trading into anti-cav.

doctrines.name: Devastation
doctrines.effect: Increases DMG dealt to units by 120, increases all types of DMG by 80.
doctrines.note: disputed — Sipahis don't auto-attack between Croupade stomps, so a later source calls it near-useless now {2}

doctrines.name: Healing Punisher Doctrine
doctrines.effect: +20% DMG to targets currently regenerating health.

veterancy.label: Top Line
veterancy.body: Recommended over Bottom because Bottom's node is bugged and doesn't function.

veterancy.label: Bottom Line
veterancy.body: Used instead to stack all available damage bonuses — charge before losing Croupade adds a 15% damage bonus from this line; no bug mentioned.

battleRole.positioning: Wait until the enemy has just finished dealing their brace/stomp damage, then trigger Impassioned so every model leaps again — including ones still mid-air — for roughly double leap damage in one move; follow up with Croupade to clean up if it's safe. {2} Charging in a straight line and letting the unit jump as often as possible keeps it effective; charging near a unit or barricade makes models leap in random directions instead. {2}
battleRole.tips: Croupade stomps knock down and stack a 20% defense boost per stomp for 12 seconds. {2} Quick Charge leaps trample and knock down everything hit; Impassioned's final leap hits slightly harder and applies 50% increased damage taken to everyone hit, for 4.5 seconds. {2} You can charge or Croupade into most braced formations for disruption value even without a clean kill — the exceptions are named in Matchups. {2}

numbers.label: Bottom-line damage stack
numbers.value: ~161% extra damage (10%+6%+10%+15% nodes, 30% unit trait, 50% skill, 25% mastery, 15% unit tree)

matchups.pressure: You pressure: shield units in general (charging is safe against all but Stalwarts) and simple shielded infantry, which Croupade handles well while supporting your team.

controls.notes: Press 2 (Croupade) first for its defense buff as a starter, then press 1 (Quick Charge), then the follow-up spell Quick Charge unlocks. {1} During a charge, Impassioned becomes available for a final leap dealing extra damage, knocking down everyone hit, and applying +50% damage taken for 4.5s. {2} Croupade stomps for 12 seconds, each stomp knocking down and stacking +20% defense. {2} Mastery: Croupade gains +5% damage per enemy hit, stacking 5× to +25%; Glory of Empire grants CC immunity while leaping in any skill plus reduced piercing damage taken (amount undisclosed); Cool Under Fire triggers unit-wide +defense and +movement speed for 10s on first damage taken, resetting on Croupade activation; a rare Assassin's trait grants +30% damage dealt for an unspecified duration after a Croupade kill on a hero. {2}

gaps: Veterancy line is unresolved: Amya calls Bottom Line bugged/non-functional and recommends Top Line (edited 2026-05-26); PixLNickz (2026-05-31) uses Bottom Line for damage stacking without mentioning any bug. No source reconciles this.
Two mastery-node numbers are undisclosed by developer support per the PixLNickz transcript: piercing damage reduction on Glory of Empire, and the exact duration of the Assassin's-trait damage buff.
Amya's guide has no Counters section (OP's 'Don't put' is a literal placeholder); all matchup content here comes from the PixLNickz transcript only.
No formation guidance (F1/F2 or equivalent) exists in any source.
Amya's guide was last edited 2026-05-26, pre-dating the 2026-06-25 Chaos patch anchor; doctrine/build guidance is unconfirmed against the current patch.
No house-playbook content exists for this unit — all sourcing is public-academy.

'Falconers' and 'Imperial Pikes' are the transcript's spoken names; there's no exact-match unit for the former, and two plausible Imperial pike units for the latter (Imperial Pike Guards is the only pike-classed one) - kept as-spoken rather than silently renamed.

Origin kind 'seasonal' is inferred: Amya's OP only says 'Blood of the Empire - Heroic Era', not 'Seasonal Unit' - Azaps' own write-up confirms Blood of the Empire = Season 3, used here to disambiguate.
